title: Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M — Atomic Chat on a 16 GB CPU-only laptop
slug_note: 5.63 GB GGUF on the office laptop with no GPU: it fits the ~8 GB usable RAM but decodes slowly on CPU bandwidth.

variation.quant_detail: qwen35-9b-Q4_K_M.gguf (5.63 GB, HF tree), self-quantized from Qwen's original weights with a per-tensor imatrix

engine.config: Atomic Chat app on Windows x64 or Linux x86_64, CPU backend (no NVIDIA GPU present). Model found by searching AtomicChat/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF and picking Q4_K_M. Context not stated.

requirements.notes: Estimate: 5.63 GB Q4_K_M file + short-context KV ≈ 6.5 GB resident. The tier records about 8 GB usable with Windows + a browser open, so this fits with roughly 1.5 GB to spare — the 9B is the ceiling for this box, and the tier notes call 4-bit 9B 'fits but slow'.

steps.text: Install Atomic Chat for Windows or Linux from https://atomic.chat/.
Open the app, search AtomicChat/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF, pick a quant, hit Use this model.
Start chatting; with no NVIDIA GPU the app runs the model on the CPU.

caveats: No laptop measurement recorded: status untested. The same 5.63 GB Q4_K_M artifact served as written with llama-server on our DGX Spark on 2026-11-16; that box's speeds do not carry over — expect single-digit to low-teens tok/s on CPU.
The AtomicChat GGUF repo ships text-only quants — no vision projector.
Close the browser and other apps first: Windows plus a browser already holds several of the 16 GB.
Atomic Chat has three swappable backends (see the engine record's gotchas); no speed is claimed here, so attribution does not bind.
